cards.front: Recall a key point about Natural and Manufactured Timber
cards.back: Hardwoods: broad-leaved deciduous trees - dense, strong, durable, slow-growing (30-100 years). Oak (furniture, flooring), mahogany (boat building), ash (tool handles, sports equipment).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Natural and Manufactured Timber
cards.back: Softwoods: coniferous evergreen trees - less dense, faster growing (10-30 years), easier to work. Pine (construction, furniture), cedar (outdoor, rot-resistant), spruce (structural, instruments).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Natural and Manufactured Timber
cards.back: Plywood: thin veneers glued with grain alternating at 90 degrees - prevents warping, strong in all directions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Natural and Manufactured Timber
cards.back: MDF: wood fibres bonded with resin - smooth, uniform, no grain direction, takes paint well, but dust is hazardous when cutting.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Natural and Manufactured Timber
cards.back: Chipboard: wood chips bonded with resin - economical, used for flooring and flat-pack furniture; usually veneered or laminated.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For timber questions, classify first (hardwood/softwood/manufactured), then state properties, then link to application. Mention FSC, replanting and material miles for sustainability.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Hardwoods are called hardwoods because they are always harder and stronger than softwoods. Correct: Hardwood/softwood refers to the tree type (deciduous vs coniferous), NOT wood hardness. Balsa is a hardwood but one of the softest timbers. Yew is a softwood but extremely hard and dense.
A furniture designer must choose between solid ash and plywood for a curved dining chair seat. Evaluate both materials and justify your selection.

AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). For grade 9, demonstrate detailed knowledge of timber categories and perceptive evaluation of material suitability.
